searchText: <GuthL> Hi, in the context of Stateless Ethereum, are miners expected to keep the state? No Yes, but in the context of Re-Genesis - No 🙂 <GuthL> Thanks Alexey. That's what I thought. I guess from my readings, that in ReGenesis, miners would have to keep the state within an epoch. Yes, that's right. I have not yet thought about how to make sure the "coinbase" account gets proven after each ReGenesis. Perhaps we'll have to introduce a "fake" transaction for that <GuthL> You mean, right after? at any point after. If the miner mines the block, and it is the first block mined that miner, we need to somehow insert merkle proof of the coinbase into the "active state" otherwise we cannot credit the block reward. The same for uncle rewards, of course <GuthL> I don't see it to be a problem. Technically, the state commitment in the header, at the ReGenesis height, is also the merkle root of the ReGenesis state. Because the miner needs to provide a witness for the block leading to the ReGenesis block, its own inclusion is proven I do not see it as a problem either, but it needs some kind of special handling https://etherscan.io/block/10550583 This empty block just happened. I dont check often, what makes empty blocks happen? perhaps it was 2 blocks mined in the same second <timbeiko> Miners start mining as soon as they get a new block and gradually add txns from their pool to the block, I believe. I assume this means a miner found a block very quickly after the next block.
